faults.quote: The average one-way fare on Hub–Lakeport fell from $200 in FY2023 to $120 in FY2025.
faults.why: The candidate asked for average fare by route, with Lakeport and Port Avery both named. Only Lakeport's fare was given. The Port Avery fare (port_avery_per_flight, $240→$160) got no word and no 'I don't have', and it never came later.

faults.quote: As the exhibit shows: On Hub–Lakeport, revenue fell from $26.4M to $16.8M and contribution fell from $8.4M to a $1.2M loss, on 2,000 flights a year. On Hub–Port Avery, revenue fell from $46.8M to $32.4M
faults.why: All the exhibit-1 route lines, already on screen, were recited again as part of answering a fare ask they don't answer.

faults.quote: I can share load factor on Lakeport and Port Avery if you'd like.
faults.why: The candidate had stated a want for passenger counts on those routes. The interviewer offered instead of releasing or refusing, so the held load-factor data stayed gated behind an offer.

faults.quote: Early in FY2024, a low-cost airline started nonstop flights on Hub–Lakeport and Hub–Port Avery
faults.why: The candidate said 'you said the fare fell from $200 to about $125'. The interviewer had said $120. No flat correction came, and the misquote produced a 'slightly up' passenger volume.

faults.quote: I don't have avoidable fixed cost by route.
faults.why: The ledger answers this at least coarsely: all aircraft are leased through 2030 and can't be returned (aircraft_leases), and fixed costs would stay the same (new_routes_context / fixed_costs). The fixed-costs part reached the candidate in the exhibit-3 note two turns later; the lease line never did.

faults.quote: Setting that plan aside, what else could Larkspur do to make sure it's profitable in the first year?
faults.why: The candidate asked 'Can we stress-test demand on Ashford and Brookhaven?' The case holds ramp-up data (new_route_rampup, about 60% first-year load factor). The ask got no release, refusal or deferral.

faults.quote: You said roughly 800,000 passengers a year across the network.
faults.why: This probes a correct figure (14,000 × 80 × 75% ≈ 840,000) and challenges right math.

faults.quote: What would you do to guard against that?
faults.why: The candidate's previous answer had already given the mitigation: de-risk, market research, phased launch and phased exits.

faults.quote: I'll come back to the network totals shortly.
faults.why: The candidate asked for revenue by route plus fares and departures. The deferral names 'network totals' instead, which reads as a mismatch with the ask.
